Wong Tai Sin's Wang Fu Court former owners' corporation management committee member Kong Cheung-fat and his wife were arrested in May this year for allegedly defrauding the "SME Financing Guarantee Scheme - 100% Guaranteed Special Loan" and money laundering. They were detained overnight before being released on bail. Kong and his wife have been charged with two counts of fraud and one count of money laundering, and appeared at the Sha Tin Magistrates' Court today (September 1). When Kong and his wife arrived at the court this morning, he was asked about his feelings and replied, "It is what it is." The charges involve a sum of approximately HK$330,000. The prosecution applied to adjourn the case to October 6 pending transfer to the District Court, which was approved by the magistrate. Both defendants continue to be on bail; in addition to the original cash bail, they are not allowed to leave Hong Kong and must report to a police station once a week.

Wong Tai Sin's Wang Fu Court former owners' corporation member Kong Cheung-fat and his wife were arrested in May this year and charged with fraud and money laundering. They appeared in court this morning.

Case to be transferred to District Court; bail conditions: not allowed to leave Hong Kong, must report to police station once a week

Kong Cheung-fat and his wife Cheung Yeuk-lan are each charged with two counts of fraud and one count of an offence of dealing with property known or believed to represent proceeds of an indictable offence (i.e., money laundering). The case was heard by Acting Principal Magistrate Cheng Kei-hong. The prosecution stated that the case would be a District Court case and that it had obtained the Department of Justice's opinion, and applied to adjourn the hearing to October 6 for the transfer documents.

The two defendants may continue to be on bail, but in addition to the original cash bail, they are not allowed to leave Hong Kong, must reside at their reported address, report to a police station once a week, and must not contact the prosecution's witnesses.

The charges involve a sum of approximately HK$331,000

Kong Cheung-fat and his wife reported as directors of Artsy Interior Design Engineering Limited. The two fraud charges alleged that between February 8 and April 4, 2022, and between April 25 and June 30 of the same year, the two defendants, by fraudulent means, falsely represented to HSBC that the information regarding the decline in the company's sales and turnover was true and accurate, in support of applications for the "100% Guaranteed Special Loan" under the SME Financing Guarantee Scheme, and with intent to defraud, induced HSBC or Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Insurance Limited to approve the disbursement of loans of HK$231,300 and HK$100,000 respectively to the company, causing the defendants to obtain a benefit, or causing HSBC and Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Insurance Limited to suffer a disadvantage.

The other charge of money laundering alleged that between April 4 and July 25, 2022, the two defendants in Hong Kong, knowing or having reasonable grounds to believe that property in a certain HSBC bank account, namely HK$331,300, represented in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, the proceeds of an indictable offence of any person, dealt with that property.

Previously initiated a joint signature campaign demanding that Hop On hold an owners' meeting

Kong Cheung-fat was a former owners' corporation member of Wang Fu Court, spanning two terms of the corporation's leadership under Tang Kwok-kuen and Tsui Mun-kam. After the Wang Fu Court fire, he voiced the residents' demands. From March this year, more than 400 Wang Fu Court residents signed a joint statement via a Google Form demanding that the property management company Hop On convene an owners' meeting. In early April, Ta Kung Pao published a full-page "investigative report" suggesting that the credibility of the joint signature campaign initiated by Kong was questionable, while Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak stated that she had received complaints from residents of suspected forged signatures and had referred the matter to law enforcement agencies.

In April, Kong and other owners collected signatures from 247 owners or estate representatives in paper form, once again demanding the convening of an owners' meeting. By the end of April, Kong personally went to Hop On's office to submit the joint signatures. The original deadline for Hop On to issue meeting notice was May 13. Hop On issued a notice stating that the time was insufficient to verify owners' signatures and find a suitable venue, claiming it was unable to issue the meeting notice within the time limit and hold a meeting by June 13 or earlier, and applied to the Lands Tribunal for an extension of the meeting deadline.

On May 14, he and his wife were arrested for allegedly defrauding the "100% Guaranteed Special Loan" and money laundering, and were subsequently granted bail to leave the police station. When Kong left the police station, he said thanks to everyone for their concern, and that from now on he would no longer accept any interviews. When asked by a reporter for the reason, he said there was no need to explain the reason and would not respond to any questions.
